_README: Kit-blessed TanStack versions, and what each distilled reference was written against.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: TanStack publishes no LTS. No `lts` dist-tag on any package,
no support-window policy — just one rolling line per library. There is no upstream
stability signal to defer to, so THIS FILE IS THE LTS: the kit blesses one version
per package and every project runs it. One project upgrades = all projects upgrade,
EXACT VERSIONS, NOT RANGES. A caret range lets a fresh install drift to a version
the kit never blessed, defeating lockstep silently.
reads manifests only, never the network.
MOVING A PIN is /review-tanstack: read what changed between our version and latest,
decide whether it affects how WE use TanStack, and if we take the bump, update the
references it invalidates. Never bump this file to make a build pass.

_packages_notes.@tanstack/react-table: v9.0.0, GA 2026-08-04 after 54 alphas + 80 betas. v8 is NOT the conservative alternative — its last release was 8.21.3 on 2025-04-14. Do not use legacyCreateColumnHelper: open upstream TS issue (aggregationFn rejects built-in string identifiers).
_packages_notes.@tanstack/react-router-ssr-query: Glue package. Sole export setupRouterSsrQueryIntegration({router, queryClient}) — wires QueryClientProvider plus SSR dehydrate/hydrate/streaming. Required wherever Query is used with Start.
_packages_notes.@tanstack/react-form-start: Start integration for Form: formOptions, createServerValidate, getFormData, mergeForm. Versioned in lockstep with react-form.

banned.react-hook-form: Use @tanstack/react-form. NOTE: `npx shadcn add form` installs this as a hard dependency — do not use shadcn's form atom; build field components against TanStack Form instead.

_form_rule: Form-library adoption is decided PER APP, all-in within an app. Three states,
and the third is a hard failure:
1. app declares @tanstack/react-form           -> decided, nothing to record
2. app listed in FORM_LIB_EXEMPT_APPS          -> deliberately decided no
3. app in neither                              -> question never asked, FAIL
FORM_LIB_EXEMPT_APPS is a space-separated app-name list in
.claude/sync-substitutions.json, read at runtime (same shape as DEPLOY_WORKFLOWS).
Exempt suits apps with no real data entry — ecommerce/cart surfaces, marketing
pages, and control-plane/service apps whose UI is a couple of status screens.
Data-entry apps (ERP browses and record forms) take the library.

_references_notes: DISTILLED, not copied. Our subset in our words, scoped to what business
applications need. `distilled_from` records which upstream skills were read, so
/review-tanstack knows what to re-read when a pin moves; an empty list means
there is no upstream for it.
NOT CARRIED, deliberately: every migrate-* skill (one-offs — SKILL.md says where
to read one), server-components (we do not use RSC), offline persistence,
SCOPE RULE: if we do not use a feature, it does not get pages explaining how the
feature works. Upstream already documents it and node_modules already has it.

@tanstack/query-intent.why: TanStack/query PR #10879 (draft since 2026-06-04) adds 29 Query skills in a NEW @tanstack/query-intent package — not inside react-query. Query is currently the largest area with no upstream at all, so queries-and-mutations.md is written from scratch.
@tanstack/query-intent.action: When it publishes, re-distil queries-and-mutations.md against it and keep only our decisions on top.

@tanstack/react-table.why: v9.0.0 was 2 days old when blessed. Watch 9.0.1/9.1 and issues touching what we use: manualPagination, column visibility/order, row selection.
@tanstack/react-table.action: Bump on the next review if patches have landed.

start-middleware.why: We deliberately do NOT use createMiddleware for auth (server-functions.md). #2783 — server middleware in the client bundle — was open Nov 2024 to Feb 2026. Still open: #7213 (middleware calling a server function in another file throws) and #7459 (createMiddleware undefined on cold-start SSR in vite dev, filed against 1.168.9).
start-middleware.action: If both close, the technical objection is gone — but the decision still needs a reason to adopt beyond saving lines. Middleware's only real capability over a handler-top call is running code AFTER the handler. Re-open only when something genuinely needs wrapping.
